content.title: Bargaining over price (markets and small shops) — Vegetable Seller (A1)

context.setting: Your vegetable stall at a local market. Today's tomatoes are ₹50 a kilo. You can offer ₹45 for one kilo.
context.learnerRole: Vegetable Seller; you own and run the stall alone.
context.objective: State a price, politely refuse a low offer, and agree a price for one kilo of tomatoes.
constraints: Use only the prices and stock given in each practice.
Agree only an offer you can make at your own stall.
Make no health, pesticide or certification claims.

keyExpressions.note: Say the price and the amount.
Give a price you can accept.

vocabulary.definition: A red vegetable sold at the stall.
The money you ask for an item.
The lowest price you can offer here.
vocabulary.example: My best price is ₹45 a kilo.

notes: ₹ means rupees. These prices are for this practice.
Listen for the price per kilo, not just the number.

items.q: The customer asks the price. Tomatoes are ₹50 a kilo.
The customer offers ₹40. Your lowest price is ₹45 a kilo. Offer that price.

rolePractice.instructions: Work in pairs. Read your own card. Ask, offer and reply. Agree a price. Then change roles.

cards.goal: Sell one kilo of tomatoes at a price you can accept.
cards.info: Start at ₹50 a kilo. You can accept ₹45, but not ₹40.
Offer ₹40 first. Ask for the best price. You can accept ₹45.

performanceTask.prompt: Neel wants one kilo of tomatoes. In this new practice, your price is ₹60 a kilo and your lowest price is ₹55. Neel offers ₹50, then accepts ₹55. Speak as the seller without reading the model.

selfCheck: Did I say the price per kilo?
Did I stay within my given prices?
Did I confirm the final amount and price?

reviewRetrieval.prompt: Later, cover the model. Say a polite refusal.

answerKey.answer: Possible seller replies: ₹60 a kilo. / Sorry, I cannot do that. / I can offer ₹55. / One kilo for ₹55.

content.title: Discussing quantity, weight and measures — Vegetable Seller (A1)

context.setting: Your vegetable stall. Potatoes are sold by weight. Onions are also available as individual small or large ones.
context.learnerRole: Vegetable Seller; you own and run the stall alone.
context.objective: Ask how much the customer wants and confirm weight, number and size.
constraints: Use only the vegetables and amounts given in each practice.
Check unclear amounts before confirming the order.
Make no health, pesticide or certification claims.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Two small ones or two large ones?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Half a kilo and two large onions.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Two large onions, as you asked.

keyExpressions.text: Two small ones or two large ones?

vocabulary.definition: A vegetable often sold by weight.
vocabulary.example: Half a kilo of potatoes, please.

vocabulary.definition: A short word for kilogram; a unit of weight.

vocabulary.example: These potatoes weigh half a kilo.

notes: Use 'how much' for weight and 'how many' for a number of items.

items.q: A customer wants potatoes. You need the weight.
The customer wants half a kilo of potatoes and two large onions. Say both amounts.

answers: Half a kilo of potatoes and two large onions.

rolePractice.instructions: Work in pairs. Ask about weight, number and size. Repeat the complete order. The customer checks it. Then change roles.

cards.goal: Find out and confirm the order.
cards.info: You have potatoes and small or large onions. Ask for any missing amount or size.
Start with 'Potatoes and onions, please.' You want half a kilo of potatoes and two large onions. Give the amounts when asked.

performanceTask.prompt: A customer says, 'Potatoes and onions, please.' Ask for the missing details. Your partner wants one kilo of potatoes and three small onions. Confirm the complete order without reading the model.
successCriteria: Ask for the number of onions.
Confirm one kilo of potatoes and three small onions.

selfCheck: Did I ask 'how much' about weight?
Did I ask 'how many' about number?
Did I repeat the correct order?

reviewRetrieval.prompt: Later, cover the model. Ask about the weight a customer wants.
Ask about the number of onions.
reviewRetrieval.answer: How many onions do you want?

answerKey.answer: Half a kilo of potatoes and two large onions.
Possible replies: How much do you need? / How many onions do you want? / Small ones or large ones? / One kilo of potatoes. Three small onions.

content.title: Taking payment (cash, UPI, card) — Vegetable Seller (A1)

context.setting: Your vegetable stall. Dev's potatoes cost ₹40 and onions cost ₹20: ₹60 in total. This stall accepts cash and UPI, but not cards.
context.learnerRole: Vegetable Seller; you own and run the stall alone.
context.objective: State the total, discuss the available payment methods, and confirm change or a known payment result.
constraints: Use only the prices and payment facts given in each practice.
Do not say a UPI payment is received unless the practice says it is confirmed.
Give no financial, regulatory or payment-system advice.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes. Cash or UPI is fine.

keyExpressions.note: Say which payment methods are available.

vocabulary.definition: Money returned when someone pays more than the total.
A written record of a payment.
A digital payment method used in India.

notes: In the model, ₹100 minus ₹60 is ₹40 change.
UPI means Unified Payments Interface. Practise payment communication, not how to use an app.

items.q: The total is ₹60. The customer gives you ₹100.
The UPI payment of ₹60 is confirmed as received. Choose your reply.
options: Your ₹60 payment is received. Thank you.

answers: Your ₹60 payment is received. Thank you.

items.q: The customer asks, 'Can I pay by card?' Your stall accepts cash and UPI only.

rolePractice.instructions: Work in pairs. State the total and payment methods. Take the customer's cash, say the change and give a receipt. Then change roles.

cards.info: The total is ₹75. You accept cash and UPI. For this practice, the customer gives you ₹100 cash. You have ₹25 change and a receipt.

cards.goal: Pay for the vegetables and get a receipt.
cards.info: Ask the total and whether cash is accepted. Give ₹100 cash. Ask for a receipt.

performanceTask.prompt: The vegetables total ₹90. Your stall accepts cash and UPI only. Your partner asks to pay by card, then gives you ₹100 cash. You have ₹10 change and a receipt. Complete the payment conversation without reading the model.

selfCheck: Did I state the correct total?
Did I name only the available methods?
Did I say the correct change?

reviewRetrieval.prompt: Later, cover the model. Ask the customer's payment method.
The total is ₹90 and the customer pays ₹100. Say the change.

answerKey.answer: Your ₹60 payment is received. Thank you.
Possible seller replies: That is ₹90, please. / Sorry, cash or UPI only. / Here is your ₹10 change. / Here is your receipt.
